What if reading your notes again is the reason you forget them?
Most students reread before an exam, and it feels like it works.
The page looks familiar, so your brain says, I know this.
But familiar isn't the same as remembered.
In one experiment, students read a passage four times.
A week later, they remembered forty percent.
Others read it once, then tried to recall it three times.
Pulling an answer out of your head is what makes the memory stronger.
Rereading only shows you the same page again.
So close the notebook, and ask yourself what you just read.
Struggling to remember isn't failing. It's how you learn.
